scenes.name: Queue Flood

say: Same rule, over and over. Except that login.
The queue's loud so you'll miss a real one.
That login's wrong. I'm opening it.
Muting the broken rule. It can wait.
Fair. Just don't go deaf on me.
Clean isn't the same as safe.
And the weird login scrolls away. Classic.

scenes.shot_notes: Alert banners stack on the player's screens while Marcus leans over the chair and taps one row.

scenes.name: Binders

say: Welcome to the quiet side. The fires here burn slower.
Slower, and they come with signatures.
Brindlecove runs our payroll in their cloud.
Their security report came back with exceptions.

beats.caption: Exception: former staff kept system access for weeks after leaving.
Exception: backup restores were never tested this year.

say: Payroll runs Friday. Procurement wants a signature today.
Your desk now. Tell me how you'd play it.
Sign it. They commit to a fix date, in writing.
A date on paper. I'll file it where we can find it.
Dates slip. Somebody has to check.

options.rem: Nadia will remember you signed it.

say: No signature until they close the access gap.
Procurement will call that slow. I'll call it defensible.

options.rem: Dana will remember you held the line.

say: This is above my desk. Accepting that risk is your call.
Fair. Risk gets accepted by an owner. Learn who owns what.

options.rem: Dana will remember you passed it up.

say: Procurement heard silence as a yes. It's signed.

options.rem: Nadia will remember the empty signature line.

say: Every signature in this room is a promise somebody made.

scenes.location: The risk and compliance office, morning, year two
scenes.shot_notes: Dana drops a thick binder on an empty desk by the window. Nadia stands behind her with a coffee and a pen.

scenes.name: Day One

say: Welcome to the loft. That's the admin console.
And that sticky note is everyone's password.

beats.caption: ADMIN CONSOLE. One shared login. No second factor.

say: Investor demo tomorrow. Please don't break anything.
Whatever you want to fix, put it on the list.
Named accounts and a second factor. Today, before the demo.
So the demo login takes longer. Charming.
New password, three people, no sticky notes. MFA next week.
A compromise. I'll pretend it was my idea.
After the demo. Top of the list, I promise.
The list is where tickets go to retire.
Also, sales needs admin for the demo. Sales is me.
I'll set up a demo copy with fake customers. No real data.
Fake customers. Finally, ones who call back.
You get your own login. Read only. It still shows everything.
Read only. Like a museum. Fine.
Fine. Admin. Don't click anything red.
Everything in here is red. I'll be brave.
I'll take that as the sticky note.

beats.caption: The demo goes fine. Nobody asks about the login screen.

scenes.shot_notes: Brick walls, folding tables, a beanbag nobody trusts. Jordan taps a sticky note stuck to a monitor. Theo talks while walking past.

scenes.name: The Brochure

say: We stop zero-days before they exist.
Your team can stop thinking so hard.
Miracle, or a brochure. Hard to tell.
Run it on our logs. No slides.
If it only works on slides, it doesn't.
We'll take it. I'm done with the noise.
Hope the magic comes with a receipt.
You'll call when the queue wins.
Quiet reads as yes. The rep heard yes.

scenes.location: Harborline Financial, a small conference room, the following week
scenes.shot_notes: A vendor rep smiles and slides a glossy one-pager across the table. Marcus keeps his hands off it.

scenes.name: The Exception

beats.caption: Access review: executives exempt from MFA. Approved by IT. No end date.

say: The exception. I know. Everyone hates the exception.
My leaders were tapping phones in board meetings. It slowed them down.
They're the busiest people here. Pick a fight somewhere else.

options.t: Write it up as a finding

say: It's a finding. The most targeted logins have the least protection.
Bold, for the new desk. Spell my name right.
See? You're easy to work with.

then.caption: The exception stays in the register. No owner. No end date.

options.rem: Priya will remember you let it go.

say: Keep it till next quarter. Then faster MFA, or it's a finding.
A deadline and a better tool. Fine. I'll hold you to the tool.
Great talk. Close the door on your way out.

scenes.shot_notes: Priya types without looking up. You hold a one-page memo. Her screen shows a calendar packed edge to edge.

scenes.name: One AM

beats.caption: ALERT: Cloud access key found in a public code repository.
Pushed tonight. Commit message: "quick fix, will clean up later."
The key can read and write the payments storage.

say: Mm. Is the site down? Don't take the site down.
Customers in other time zones are buying right now.
Killing the key now. The site blinks for a few minutes.
A few minutes. I'm timing you.
I'll make the repo private and rotate first thing tomorrow.
Smart. Nobody reads code at one in the morning.

then.caption: Automated scanners do. They never sleep.

say: Your call. Downtime now, or a live key until morning.
You're the security person. That's why I hired you. Rotate it.
You're staring at it. Is staring a fix?

beats.caption: Morning. The engineer who pushed it writes: "my fault, so sorry."

say: Do we fire someone? Investors like a firm hand.
No. We scan for secrets before every push. Tired people make mistakes.
Robots babysitting engineers. Fine. Cheaper than hiring.
Formal warning. People need to see a consequence.
Great. Now nobody admits anything to you ever again.
No answer. I'll let it slide. Again.

scenes.shot_notes: The loft is dark except your laptop. Your phone buzzes across the table. Theo is asleep in a desk chair under one lamp and jolts awake.

scenes.name: The New Hire

say: If I close this, am I gonna make it worse?
You sat in that chair once. Your call.
Pull up a chair. We'll walk it slow.
Hand it over. I'll close this one.

scenes.shot_notes: A new hire hovers at the player's shoulder, notepad clenched, while Marcus watches from the next desk.

scenes.name: The Examiner

say: Joan Mercer. I've read a lot of plans. Most are lovely.
Show me proof the bank tests its incident response plan.
Answer what she asked. Nothing more, nothing less.
Our last exercise. Who attended, what we decided, the gaps we found.
Gaps, written down. That's rarer than you'd think.

options.rem: Joan Mercer will remember the records.

say: Here's the full plan. It's very thorough.
I asked for a test. This is a document.

options.rem: Joan Mercer will remember the binder.

say: All of it. Plans, logs, emails. Take your pick.
Now she reads everything. Including what we haven't.

options.rem: Nadia will remember the paper avalanche.

say: I'll note the evidence was not readily available.

options.rem: Joan Mercer will remember the wait.

say: When the plan failed in practice, who updated it?
Nobody, yet. It's open, with an owner and a date.
Honest and tracked. I can live with tracked.

options.rem: Joan Mercer will remember the honest answer.

say: Then send me the updated version by Friday.
We don't have an updated version.
The update is in progress. We'll share the tracking record.
Next time, the person who owns it answers.

options.rem: Joan Mercer will remember who answered.

say: Silence is an answer. I'll write it down as one.

options.rem: Joan Mercer will remember the silence.

say: I'm not here to catch you. I'm here to see if you'd catch yourselves.

scenes.location: A glass conference room, morning, year three
scenes.shot_notes: Joan Mercer sits alone at the long table with a legal pad. Nadia sits beside you. A stack of folders waits in front of you.

scenes.name: The Questionnaire

beats.caption: From a big bank prospect: Security Questionnaire. Due Friday.

say: Biggest deal we've ever chased. I can taste it.
Also my commission. I can taste that too.
Every answer is yes. Yes reads like confidence.

beats.caption: Do you encrypt all customer data at rest?
Do you test backups and run a written incident plan?

say: We will. Eventually. Future tense is still yes.
We answer what's true today. Every gap gets a fix date.
Honest and broke. My parents will be so proud.
Let me call their security people. A gap sounds better with a plan.
Talking to customers. Bold. Fine, set it up.
Yes to everything. I'll make it true before they check.
That's the spirit. That's the whole startup spirit.
Silence. I'll type the yeses myself.

beats.caption: The questionnaire goes out Friday afternoon.

say: We'll probably win it. Why does it feel like lying in a nice font?

scenes.location: Kestrel Pay loft, day, months later
scenes.shot_notes: A long spreadsheet fills the wall screen. Jordan bounces on the beanbag. Theo stands with arms crossed, smiling a little too much.

scenes.name: The Page

say: If it buzzes again, I'm throwing it out.
Tell work the night shift moved out.
Good. I'll bring the ugly parts.
Sam, can you take this? I'm cooked.
Yeah. Sleep. I'll ping you at daylight.
Bold. Your work friends will love that.
Page died. I'm starting without you.

scenes.location: The player's apartment, two in the morning
scenes.shot_notes: Jordan squints from the couch. The player is still in yesterday's clothes as the phone buzzes and lights the room.

scenes.name: The Tabletop

beats.caption: Exercise scenario: file servers encrypted. A ransom note on every screen.

say: Okay. Files are locked. We're, uh, isolating?
Isolating what? Payments still have to run.
So who says pull the plug? Me? Priya?
Facilitator. The room is stuck. Move it.
The plan names who decides. Who is it?
It says incident commander. We never named one.

options.rem: Dana will remember you used the plan.

say: Isolate now. I'll take the heat.
In a real incident, you don't have that authority.

options.rem: Priya will remember you grabbed the wheel.

say: Pause. Nobody here knows who decides. That's the finding.
We just argued away the afternoon. Is that the exercise?
This is what exercises are for. Better here than on a Saturday.
Now. What goes in the after-action report?
Every gap. No decider, no contact list, no backup check.
Good. Gaps with owners turn into fixes.

options.rem: Dana will remember the honest report.

say: Lessons learned. Nothing that reads like failure.
Finally, a report I can forward.
And a report nobody can act on.

options.rem: Priya will remember the friendly report.

say: We note who hesitated. People need to own it.
Cool. Next time I'll just stay quiet. Safer.
If it isn't written down, it didn't happen. Write it.

options.rem: Dana will remember the blank page.

scenes.location: The incident war room, afternoon, year three
scenes.shot_notes: You stand at the whiteboard holding a marker. Sam, Priya and Dana sit around the table. A fake ransom note glows on the wall screen.

scenes.name: Ship It

say: Saved cards ship tonight. One click checkout.
Encryption is next sprint. One sprint, tops.

beats.caption: Card numbers would sit in the database as plain text.

say: Release goes in ten minutes. Yes or no?
No. Plain text card numbers don't ship. Not even for one night.
You just cost me a launch post. Fine. Next sprint.
Ship it to staff accounts only. Real customers wait for encryption.
A soft launch. Investors love that phrase anyway.
Ship it. Encryption is the first ticket next sprint.
That's why you're here. To say yes faster.

then.caption: The next sprint comes. So does the one after that.

say: Clock ran out. Shipping. Be mad tomorrow.

then.caption: The next sprint comes. So does the one after that.

scenes.shot_notes: Pizza crusts and a release countdown on the wall screen. Theo leans over your desk with a launch checklist. The encryption box is unchecked.

scenes.name: Bad Monday

say: Files are locked. There's a note on the screen.
Who calls it? I, uh, blanked.
The clock is the lesson. Talk.
We cut the network. Then we brief you plain.
Plain works. Do it that way when it's real.
We pay the note. We buy the day back.
Sam, your room. Make the call.
Right. Isolate first. I should've led with that.
Nobody spoke. That's how a bad Monday starts.
What failed first? The tools, or this room?
The alerts cried wolf. We went numb.
That's the day job sneaking in. True, though.
We froze. That's on this room.
Good. I can work with a room that admits it.
You went quiet. I still counted that.

scenes.shot_notes: Sam paces under a whiteboard of arrows, energy drink in hand. Dana waits at the head of the table. Marcus sits to the side, arms folded.

scenes.name: Soften It

beats.caption: Draft finding: backup restores untested. Recovery from ransomware is unproven. Rating: high.

say: The audit committee meets tomorrow. That line ends careers.
Change high to moderate. Say testing is in progress.
It basically is. We bought the tool.
I remember who helps me. Decide.
It stays high. I'll add that the tool is bought and a test is scheduled.
So I get credit and the bad grade. Fine.

options.rem: Priya will remember you held the rating.

say: Moderate. In progress. Just this once.

then.caption: The committee reads "moderate." Nobody asks a follow-up question.

say: Ratings aren't mine to trade. Nadia and Dana can review it.

options.rem: Priya will remember you went to legal.

say: I'll take that as a yes.

then.caption: Priya edits the line herself. Your name stays on the report.

options.rem: Priya will remember you let her type.

scenes.shot_notes: Priya shuts the door behind you and turns her laptop around. A draft audit committee report is open, one sentence highlighted.

scenes.name: Runway

say: Runway's short. The next round is late.
Your security budget, or two engineers. Pick one.
Their names are on the spreadsheet. Sorry.
Keep the engineers. I'll run on free tools and raw logs.
Noble. Also cheaper. I love both.
Cut the extras. Logging and backups stay. Those aren't up for debate.
Fine. You keep the smoke alarm. Sell the rest.
In a payments company, security is the wrong line to cut.
Then you tell them. They sit by the window.
Then I'll decide. You won't like it.

beats.caption: Later. The loft is empty. Jordan finds you on the floor.

say: You're doing the stare again. The night shift one.
Real talk. Is this place going to make it?
And did we leave holes in it on the way?
Honestly? Maybe not. But the work still counts.
Maybe not. Okay. Pass the cereal.
We'll be fine. Theo always finds money.
You blinked twice. That's your lying blink.
I'm tired. I'm the whole team, and it shows.
Then sleep. The holes will still be there tomorrow.
Okay. We just sit here, then. That's allowed.
Whatever happens, this place was safer with you in it.

scenes.shot_notes: Half the desks are empty. Theo paces with a spreadsheet on a tablet. Later, Jordan sits on the floor beside you, eating cereal from the box.

scenes.name: The Guides

say: CISSP needs five years paid before you can hold it.
CySA+ now. I want the analyst depth.
Then we use the quiet nights. If any show up.
I'll start the long reading. No rush to sit.
Good. The years still have to be real.
Not this year. The queue is the teacher.
It teaches. It also teaches bad habits.
Fine. The books can collect dust.

scenes.location: Harborline Financial, Marcus's office, months later
scenes.shot_notes: Marcus sets two exam guides on the desk and waits. The coffee beside the guides has gone cold.

scenes.name: The Letters

say: Remember the SOC? Loud room, bad coffee. Still there.
Heard you sat across from an examiner. Still breathing, I see.
Time for letters after your name. Two roads.
CISA is the auditor's cert. It fits the desk you're at.
CISSP needs five years paid. You can start the reading now.
CISA now. I want to audit like I mean it.
Good. Auditors who understand the tech are rare.

options.rem: Dana will remember you chose CISA.

say: CISSP track. Long reading, and the years keep counting.
Broad map. You'll need it for the top floor.

options.rem: Marcus will remember you chose the long road.

say: Not this year. I need some evenings back.
Fair. Rested people write better findings.

options.rem: Dana will remember you needed a breather.

say: Shrug noted. The guides make nice coasters.
Back to the noise for me. Visit sometime.
One more thing. Close the door.
A promotion conversation is coming. Be ready to want something.

beats.caption: Dana doesn't say which job. She says to think about it.

scenes.location: Dana's office, late afternoon, year four
scenes.shot_notes: Dana sits behind her desk. Marcus leans in the doorway in a SOC hoodie, two study guides tucked under his arm.

scenes.name: The Buyer

beats.caption: Harborline Financial has acquired Kestrel Pay.

say: Dana Whitfield, Harborline security. We just bought your startup.
Part of the deal is you. We want you back.
Marcus says you left owing him a coffee.
Theo Grant is joining our leadership. Better you hear it from me.
Our diligence team found some holes. We'll be talking about those.
I'm in. I learned a lot building from nothing.
Good. Bring the scars. We'll put them to work.
I'll come back with a real scope, not my old seat.
Fair. You ran a whole program. Mostly alone.
Theo shipped things I told him not to ship. You should know.
Noted. Put it in writing. Facts, not feelings.
Take the quiet. Just be in the lobby Monday.
Theo got a title. We got a box. Classic.
Go on. I'll be in sales, like always.

beats.caption: Monday. The badge reader blinks green. The lobby smells the same.

scenes.location: The bank lobby, Harborline Financial, morning
scenes.shot_notes: You stand outside the lobby's glass doors, phone to your ear. Jordan hugs a box of loft junk. Final beat: you push through the doors into the lobby.

end: The queue stayed loud. You started hearing what mattered.

ends.text: You built security from nothing. Now the bank owns what you built, holes and all.
Every signature is a promise. Some of yours will come due.
The queue stayed loud. You started hearing what mattered.
